target_customer: Flatmates and tenants sharing a rental bank account
problem: Shared household money was mismanaged (late rent, unpaid groceries) when flatmates pooled funds; Glassjar tracked a flat account, ledger and payments.
business_model: Free app with a 2.9 percent fee on payments made from emailed invoices
product_category: Shared household expense and payments app

founders.name: George Smith
education: University of Canterbury (student when the company started)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CEO; NZ Inc says a pair of Canterbury students created it.

founders.name: Matt Galloway
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CTO.

founders.name: Duncan Keall
founders.background_notes: Named alongside George Smith in a 2014 Scoop release summary; not on the YC page.

exit.reason: Not public. YC lists inactive; no post-mortem found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Bank account linking and payment flows for a small team in several countries.

defensibility.rationale: Lightweight expense tracking is easy to copy and depended on bank data access.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents responding; later coverage lists Splitwise as a common flatmate tool.

market_need_then: A May 2014 release said Glassjar managed the finances of 650 rentals across New Zealand, Australia and the UK, and it launched in the US by March 2015.

branding.name_origin: Flats traditionally kept a glass jar on the bench that everyone paid into, per a search summary of 2014 coverage.

brand_strength.rationale: Name has a clear, concrete metaphor, but YC later labelled it a check writing app, and the name does not fit payments in the US. No brand press found.

pivots.to: Payments and check writing app for the US
pivots.why: Search results show a March 2015 US payments launch and a YC tagline about check writing; reason not stated

outcome_analysis: Glassjar raised about $300K through Lightning Lab and the YC standard seed in early 2015 and expanded from New Zealand to the US, but YC lists it inactive and no post-mortem, acquisition or closure report was found. The cause is not public, so no failure factor is assigned. Its funds and traction were small relative to the broad payments market it tried to enter.
notes: CB Insights lists $240K over 3 rounds including a Seed II of $0.12M on 2015-03-09 with ICE Angels, Sparkbox and Lightning Lab as other investors; NZ Inc says $300K via Lightning Lab before YC, so the figures conflict. NZ Inc article has no date. The Scoop page returned empty when fetched; its details (650 rentals, 2.9 percent fee, Keall, jar origin) come from search summaries. YC page lists no company website. Competitor list empty: no dated rival sources found, and Splitwise appears only in later coverage. Outcome search found no closure report.
